17. In view of the detailed discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and as such the accident in question had taken place.

18. ISSUE No.2:
The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and took treatment.
Petitioner has stated in the petition that, he is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
19. PAIN AND SUFFERING:
In the petition as well as in his evidence PW1 deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein he treated as an inpatient from 19.11.2023 to 22.11.2023.
The petitioner has produced the discharge card marked at Ex.P.11 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the Manipal Hospital, Bangalore for 03 days.

He has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7, which disclose that petitioner sustained fracture of both bones (radius & ulna) of the left forearm and the doctor has opined that the injuries are grievous in nature.
Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
20. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
In support of his plea, he has produced 16 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.14 to the tune of Rs.2,68,894/-.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,68,894/-
towards medical expenses.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.11 Discharge summaries issued by Manipal Hos
Hence, at least 2 months is required to recover from the accidental injuries.

So, in the absence of any evidence in respect of the income of the petitioner, the petitioner might have monthly income at Rs.16,000/-
as per the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2023 at Rs.16,000/- per mon
The accident is of the year is 2023.
Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/-p.m. as per above decision.

under this head.
22. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability-

The petitioner to prove his disability, he has produced the evidence of Dr. S. Ramachandra in order to substantiate the same, PW.3 who has opined that, total disability of whole body disability at 12.32.%.
Admittedly, the PW.3 is not a treated doctor.

Same was admitted by the PW.3 during his cross examination, the relevant evidence of the PW.3 reads as follows :
"It is true to say that, I have not personally treated the petitioner."

He was sworn that, petitioner sustained left forearm both bones (radius and ulna) fracture and further depose that, petitioner has got 12.32% disability to the whole body but he was not issued the disability certificate.
It is quite but natural that to help the petitioner doctor will give exaggerated disability.
However, looking to the nature of the injuries it is proper to came to conclusion that there is 6% of disability to the petitioner.
PW.2 is only Senior Technician, who has only produced the medical documents and his evidence is formal in nature.
23. Before proceeding on merits of the claim the age of the petitioner/injured has to be determined.
Ex.P.12 is the Aadhar card of the petitioner, wherein year of birth is mentioned as 1954 and accident took place in the year 2023.
Accordingly, I assess his age as 69 years at the time of this accident.
As per the ruling reported in AIR 2009 SCW page-3014 between SARLA VERAMA AND OTHERS VS DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS, the relevant multiplier applicable is '5'.
Under this head the petitioner is entitled for an amount of Rs.57,600/-.

24. FOOD, CONVEYANCE, NOURISHMENT AND ATTENDANT CHARGES:
Further the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as inpatient in Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru as inpatient from 19.11.2023 to 22.11.2023 i.e. for total 03 day
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of nutritious food and attendant charges.
25. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The petitioner was aged about 69 years at the time of accident, he has sustained grievous injuries.
It shows that he found difficulty in doing day to day works.
He might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life.
Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.20,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness.

The respondent No.2 admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

ORDER
